previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis following fundoplication was admitted for a one-day episode of severe nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She reported bloody streaks in her vomit, but examination and labs showed no active bleeding, with stable hemoglobin and prior findings of esophagitis and esophageal ulcer on recent EGD. CT scan ruled out bowel obstruction and showed stable SMA dissection and a small, unchanged adrenal nodule. She presented with anion gap metabolic acidosis and mild hypokalemia, both resolved with IV fluids and repletion. Bowel rest, IV antiemetics, and gradual restart of enteral feeds led to symptom resolution. She was discharged home on her prior medications with instructions to advance tube feeds and follow up with her PCP regarding the adrenal nodule.

ACUTE ISSUES:
# Nausea/Intractable vomiting: The patient presented with 2 days 
of nausea, vomiting, and increased bowel movements. Differential 
included gastroparesis flare with diarrhea from lactose 
intolerance, gastroenteritis, infectious colitis. Pancreatitis, 
SBO and mesenteric ischemia less likely (lipase 36, no 
peritoneal signs on abd exam). Presentation appears similar to 
previous admission, pt reports eating milk products over weekend 
which usually cause transient diarrhea. Had low grade temp to 
100.3 on admission, resolved without antipyretics. Was 
maintained NPO with IVF and IV metoclopramide, ondasentron and 
lorazepam. Enteral feeds where started on HD 3 per nutrition 
recommendations, the patient tolerated these well and was 
started on a clear liquid diet overnight. Diet was not advanced 
further while inpatient.
.  
# Metabolic Acidosis: Presented with AG metabolic acidosis with 
HCO3 of 15 and AG of 21. UA was positive for 150 ketones. With 
fluids, AG and HCO3 normalized. Pt does not have DM (last HgA1c 
not elevated). Likely due to starvation. Last tube feeding was 
___. 
.
# Esophagitis: Reported self-inducing vomiting multiple times in 
the past several days, with some bloody remnants on her finger. 
Pt was recently worked up for dysphagia and had EGD done on 
___ showing esophagitis in the gastroesophageal junction and 
distal esophagus, esophageal ulceration at GE junction. Biopsies 
were benign. There were no signs of bleeding throughout 
hospitalization, stool guaiac negative X1, hct drop from 41.9-> 
33.8 (Hb 14.6-11.6 O/N on ___, with repeat to 41.4 was thought 
secondary to lab error. 
.
# Hypertension: Pt presented with hypertension to 180/115, HR of 
90, denied signs/sxs of end organ damage. On the floor, vitals 
normalized. Transient hypertension likely secondary to 
hypovolemia, stress response or pain.
.
# Hypokalemia: Presented with K of 3.3, repleted as needed while 
on IV fluids. Likely due to GI losses.
.  
# Hypernatremia: Pt with Na of 146 and Cl of 115, likely due to 
volume repletion of 3 L NS. Switched to LR O/N. Resolved.  
.
# DVT Prophylaxis: maintained on SC heparin TID.
.
